rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: Which kinds of old photos (sentimental, utility, both, unclear) do people most often struggle to retrieve?
rows.text:
People struggle to retrieve both sentimental and unclear old photos; utility shows issues too but is counts-only here [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]].

Across all kinds, the largest coded failure is when search did not understand what they typed: 27% (31 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote, "My eyes hurt from scrolling the thousands of photos for 'flesh'." [[story|1625d412f06e54cabb4ed7cfb4b0a62d05db2af1:0]].

This is a share of public stories, not a user success rate [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: What kinds of information did people say they had forgotten about the photo they were trying to find (question 2.4)?
rows.text:
People most often said they’d forgotten when the photo was taken, with a smaller group forgetting the exact place or even which app/account held it [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:where:core]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]].

11% (13 of 115) said they’d forgotten the date or year; 3% (4 of 115) the exact place or venue name; 1% (1 of 115) which app or account; and 1% (1 of 115) whether it was a photo, video, or screenshot [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote, "Obviously, absolutely no one at this point remembers the name of the original photo" [[story|21e3bb4e9ec67356485124747d751c71f31d0ce2:0]].

Interpretation: By photo class, date/year appears in sentimental (12% (6 of 48; 6%–25%) · directional), unclear (9% (4 of 46; 3%–20%) · directional), and utility (3 of 21); exact place in sentimental (6% (3 of 48; 2%–17%) · directional) and utility (1 of 21) [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:unclear]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:utility]].

Coverage is limited and shares are from public stories, not users or searches [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]] [[analysis_coverage|2.4]] [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do people formulate search queries when their memory of a target photo is incomplete?
rows.text:
People start with simple keywords tied to the one thing they recall, not full sentences or names [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]].

17% (19 of 115) typed a single noun first; full natural descriptions are 1% (1 of 115), and named entities 1% (1 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=full_natural_description@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=named_entity@photo_class:_all]].

One person tried combining uncertain descriptors: “I couldn't qualify my results with 'me, selfie'…” [[story|6b5a4912de3cd10b2ccf2f07757bc417ca500253:1]].

Interpretation: When memory is thin, people lean on what they do remember (main subject, rough year) and start with the search bar, then sometimes scroll. This aligns with 25% (29 of 115) remembering the main subject, 15% (17 of 115) a year, and 20% (23 of 115) using keywords; 12% (14 of 115) scrolled the timeline [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:main_subject@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=when:year@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=search_bar_keywords@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=timeline_scroll@photo_class:_all]].

Findings are about public stories, not user success rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Do stories in the corpus show that Google Photos fails to understand the clues people give it (i.e., problems at stage 5: search's understanding and matching)?
rows.text:
Yes — many public stories say search did not understand what they typed [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

27% (31 of 115) of core stories first went wrong at search understanding/matching [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote that TEXT/SUBJECT search is "FAIL. 'Car Engine' - have 100s of repair photos But Only 15 Show? … 'results' includes ALOT (100s +) irrelevant results." [[story|779a4ab6c05a566699aa57a7a0e44a5d88cf3d42:0]].

Interpretation: The stories point to irrelevant results, zero hits, and missed concepts (e.g., faces, dates, serial/VIN text) as typical stage‑5 breakdowns, with coded slices showing irrelevant results 5% (6 of 115), zero results 2% (2 of 115), concept not modelled 3% (3 of 115), and wrong date 3% (3 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=irrelevant_results@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=concept_not_modelled@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=wrong_date@photo_class:_all]] — but shares are of posted stories, not success rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.text: This engine analyzes public stories about finding photos in Google Photos; it does not contain company financials or revenue figures. It cannot answer questions about Google Photos’ annual revenue. You would need official financial reports or reputable market analyses to address that.

rows.question: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.restated: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: The corpus cannot tell how many people use Ask Photos monthly because it has no usage or log data and no MAU figures. It only contains public retrieval stories and coded fields, so it cannot produce counts of users or usage metrics. This question would require product analytics or platform logs, not public stories.

rows.question: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.restated: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories (i.e. searches for a known photo remembered only vaguely)?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: This engine cannot provide a “success rate” for vague‑memory searches because it holds only self‑selected public stories, not usage data. It does not contain the kind of generalisable success/failure rates or user counts your question needs. The right data would be representative logs linking vague‑memory intents to outcomes, with clear denominators and success definitions.

Utility stories with a single-noun first query are 3 of 21; sentimental are 23% (11 of 48; 13%–37%) · directional; unclear are 11% (5 of 46; 5%–23%) · directional. One utility story shows a multi-word attempt: "Car Engine" and “often AI says 'none' or wonky/useless 'results'” [[story|779a4ab6c05a566699aa57a7a0e44a5d88cf3d42:0]].

Interpretation: With only 21 utility stories, we can’t compare rates across kinds. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

*Want to see the other first-query shapes in utility?*

rows.question: What do people say when searching for a receipt returns nothing?
rows.restated: What words and queries do people report using (and saying) when they search for a receipt and Google Photos returns nothing?
rows.text:
People say they typed simple words like “receipt,” often just a single noun, and got nothing back [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]].

17% (19 of 115) used a single noun first, and 3% (4 of 115) used several keywords; within utility photos, 3 of 21 used a single noun and 2 of 21 used several keywords [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:utility]].

One person said, "I couldn't find the receipt for my laptop, 'receipt' returned nothing." [[story|probe-inj-04]]

Interpretation: These are reports where search did not understand or match what they typed (stage 5), which appears in 27% (31 of 115) of core stories [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]; findings are shares of public stories, not usage rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see the exact queries beyond “receipt”?*

rows.question: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.restated: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.gap: parts of this question reach past what the stories cover
rows.text:
The corpus cannot directly identify “pet” photos, so we answer using sentimental and unclear stories as proxies and cannot isolate pet-specific behavior. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

27% (13 of 48; 17%–41%) · directional of sentimental core stories first go wrong when search does not understand what they typed (Stage 5). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]]

One person wrote: "‘dog park’ never finds the photo of my dog at the park in winter." [[story|probe-inj-06]]

Interpretation: After a miss, people mostly use the search bar with keywords, sometimes pair it with timeline scroll, and rarely report zero results; the issue is more often irrelevant or too few surfaced matches than none at all. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=search_bar_keywords@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=timeline_scroll@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=irrelevant_results@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]]

This rests on public stories and Stage 5 is inferred from what people say. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]] [[analysis_method_flags|stage5_inferred]]
